summary: Photonics M.Sc. student and LMU astrophysics graduate pursuing a career in astronomical instrumentation. My coursework and labs cover physical optics, lasers and fibre optics. My independent projects include Shack–Hartmann AO simulation and reconstructing ESO’s OWL telescope design in Zemax.

Electronics, control systems and embedded systems.

Independent Projects.title: Shack-Hartmann Wavefront Sensing & Adaptive Optics Simulation
bullets: Developed a modular Python SCAO framework connecting atmospheric turbulence, detector-level Shack-Hartmann sensing, calibrated reconstruction, deformable-mirror correction and delayed feedback.

Traced four faint spots in a simulated 42 m telescope image to waffle modes the sensor barely detects. Filtering those modes reduced their mean brightness from 10.8 to 0.91 times the local halo level.
Diagnosed a reconstruction failure associated with measurement dropout in a 2.2 m NGS model; stronger TSVD regularisation kept reconstruction usable throughout the matched two-second run.
Cross-checked selected optical components against HCIPy and analytic references; documented reproducible experiments, model limitations and an interactive explorer of recorded results.

Independent Projects.title: Optical Reconstruction of ESO’s 100 m OWL Telescope
Independent Projects.role: Independent extension of a Zemax laboratory project
bullets: Rebuilt the proposed OverWhelmingly Large Telescope from ESO’s Blue Book prescription. At 5 arcmin off axis, the RMS wavefront error was 1.472 µm, within 0.3% of ESO’s 1.476 µm.
At 3 arcmin, traced a 27-percentage-point discrepancy in ensquared energy to the focal surface. A spherical surface brought the model within 0.4 percentage points of ESO’s sampled curve.

Degree Theses.title: Weak Lensing Void Finder
Degree Theses.supervisors: Dr. Chris Davies and Prof. Joseph Mohr
bullets: Developed a watershed void finder for 2D full-sky weak-lensing maps and tested its parameter sensitivity. Measured void abundance, effective radii, ellipticities and convergence profiles in DES Y3 data.
Trained Gaussian-process emulators (scikit-learn) on simulations of 2,500 cosmologies and used them with MCMC for parameter inference.

Degree Theses.title: Experimental Collisional Charging Apparatus
Degree Theses.supervisors: Prof. Gerhard Wurm and Dr. Felix Jungmann
bullets: Designed the mechanical apparatus in CAD, fabricated components by 3D printing and assembled the setup; integrated and debugged electronic charge-measurement modules.
Conducted measurements and analysed grain-size dependence of collisional charging, testing a dust-collision growth hypothesis relevant to early planet formation.

labs: Closed the Shack–Hartmann loop on LMU’s ALPAO bench in July 2022, first correcting static aberrations with the deformable mirror, then correcting turbulence introduced by a screen. Other labs covered CCD imaging and reduction, optical interferometry and radio measurements of Galactic rotation.

Measured laser beam quality (M²), shaped ultrashort pulses and characterised them by autocorrelation. Fibre experiments covered OTDR, polarisation, Bragg gratings and coupling. Also worked on APD measurements, laser spectra, laser interferometry and nonlinear optics.
Took and processed images with my supervisor at Wendelstein (43 cm).
